question: Eku agba mi, mo ri awon leaf mi ti won n yellow, mo si ri awon small white fly ni abe leaf. Kini mo le se?
answer: Ohun ti o n se apejuwe ni eepi funfun ti gbin (Bemisia tabaci). Eepi funfun n mu 'cassava mosaic virus' wa, ati pe o le fa pipadanu ikore ti o to 70%. Ohun ti o le se: (1) Mu awon ewe ti o ni arun kuro ki o si sun won — ma ko won sinu kompositi. (2) Fun ogba kekere, lo epo neem (5 milimita fun lita omi kan) ti o fi fo labe ewe, ni gbogbo ose meje fun ose meta. (3) Gbin 'sunn hemp' tabi marigold ni eti oko — eepi funfun ko feran awon ohun ogbin wonyi. (4) Ni akoko ti nbo, gbin eya cassava ti o ni idaduro si 'cassava mosaic virus' bii TME 419 tabi TMS 98/0581. Ranti pe oogun ti o lagbara pupo le pa awon kokoro ti o n ran wa lowo, nitori naa ma lo neem tabi ose Dudu nikan. Ti o ba nilo iranlowo siwaju, lo si ile ise agbeko agbegbe re.
source: IITA Cassava Pest Management Guide, 2023; reviewed by Dr. A. Okeowo, agronomist

question: Good evening sir. My tomato leaf get black spot for underside and the fruit dey rot before e ripe. Wetin I fit do?
answer: O dey deal with late blight (Phytophthora infestans). Dis one na serious disease wey fit destroy your whole tomato farm if you no act fast. Wetin to do: (1) Remove every leaf and fruit wey don get black spot — carry them far from the farm and bury them, no put for compost. (2) Spray copper-based fungicide (copper hydroxide or copper oxychloride) at 3 grams per litre of water. Spray both top and bottom of every leaf. Repeat every 7 to 10 days if rain dey fall. Stop spraying 14 days before harvest. (3) Make your farm get good air — if the tomato plants dey too close together, thin them. (4) Next season: plant blight-resistant varieties like 'Tengeru 2010' or 'Mongal F1'. Rotate your farm — no plant tomato or potato for the same place next year. Water the ground, not the leaves, to keep the leaf dry. If you no fit get copper fungicide, ask your agricultural extension agent for help.
source: IITA Tomato Production Guide; reviewed by Dr. B. Adewale, plant pathologist

question: Sannu. Masara ta na da ramuka a cikin ganye, ina kuma ganin tsutsa a jikin ganye na sabo. Me zan yi?
answer: Wannan cuta ce da ake kira fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda), mafi hatsarin kwaro ga masara a Afirka. Kada ka damu da yawa — ana iya shawo kan ta ba tare da magunguna masu tsada ba. Abubuwan da za ka yi: (1) Idan gona karam ce, tara tsutsar da hannu a cikin mazubin masarar ka kuma ka kashe su. (2) A zuba man neem a cikin mazubin (a jiƙa ƙwayayen neem a ruwa dare daya, a tace sannan a fesa). (3) Idan gona babba ce, a yi amfani da maganin halitta kamar Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) — wannan maganin yana kashe tsutsa ne kawai, ba zai cutar da mutum ba. (4) A dasa masara da wuri, kuma a hada shi da wake-wake wanda ke rage yawan kwaro. (5) A guji amfani da magungunan kashe kwaro na roba kawai — juriya ya zama gama gari a Yammacin Afirka. Idan har yanzu kana da matsala, je ofishin noma na karamar hukumar ka.
source: FAO Fall Armyworm Control Guide, 2024; IITA Maize Program

question: Shikamoo. Mahindi yangu hayakua vizuri na majani yana rangi ya zambarau. Nilitumia mbolea ya DAP lakini haikusaidia...
answer: Shikamoo. Rangi ya zambarau kwenye majani ya mahindi inaweza kuwa na sababu nyingi — inaweza kuwa upungufu wa fosforasi, au ugonjwa wa virusi, au hata uharibifu wa mizizi kutoka kwa wadudu wa ardhini. Mimea inayoonyesha dalili za aina moja inaweza kuwa na matatizo tofauti kabisa. Kwa sababu hii, siwezi kukupa utambuzi sahihi kutoka kwa maelezo pekee. Hiki ndicho unachopaswa kufanya: Chukua mimea michache yenye dalili (pamoja na mizizi) na upeleke katika ofisi ya karibu ya kilimo ya kaunti (county extension office) au KALRO. Waambie historia yote — tarehe ya kupanda, mbolea uliyotumia, na mwelekeo wa dalili. Watachunguza na kukupa ushauri sahihi. Usitumie dawa yoyote kabla ya kupata utambuzi sahihi — inaweza kuwa upotevu wa pesa na inaweza kuharibu mazingira.
source: KALRO Maize Diagnostics Protocol; FAO Guide to Nutrient Deficiency Identification

question: Namaste. Dhaan ki pattiyon par bhooray dhabbe hain aur baal aur baal ke dono taraf piliyaan dikh rahi hain. Kya karna chahiye?
answer: Yeh rice blast rog hai (Magnaporthe grisea), jo chawal ki fasal ke liye sabse khatarnak bimariyon mein se ek. Yeh fungus pattiyon, daathon aur danon ko bhi prabhavit kar sakta hai. Iska ilaaj: (1) Prabhavit pattiyon ko turant kaat kar hata dein aur khet se door jala dein. (2) Khet mein paani bhar kar rakhein — fungus pani mein phail nahi sakta. (3) Tricyclazole ya carbendazim-based fungicide ka chidakav karein, 10-14 din ke antraal par, agar bimari zyada faili hai. (4) Agli fasal ke liye: roti pratirodhak kismein lagayein jaise 'Pusa 44' ya 'Swarna', aur beej ko seed treatment avashya karein. (5) Ure ki matra ko sambhal kar rakhein — zyada nitrogen se blast bimari badh jaati hai. Khoon ki kami ho to potash ki matra badha dein. Kshetriya krishi vistar adhikari se sampark karein agar bimari 40% se adhik phasal tak phail gayi hai.
source: ICAR Rice Blast Management Guide, 2024; Punjab Agricultural University

question: Good morning. My cowpea leaves are curling and I see small black insects on the stems and young pods. What can I use that is safe?
answer: The small black insects on stems and pods are cowpea aphids (Aphis craccivora). While they rarely kill the plant by themselves, they transmit mottle virus which can reduce yield by 60%. Here is a safe management plan: (1) For small infestations (less than 20% of plants): spray with neem oil at 5ml per litre of water, or make a soap solution (1 tablespoon of mild liquid soap in 1 litre of water). (2) For larger infestations: apply a botanical insecticide like pyrethrum-based spray. Avoid broad-spectrum synthetic insecticides — they kill the predators that naturally control aphids. (3) Plant a border of sorghum or maize around your cowpea field — this attracts ladybirds and hoverflies that eat aphids. (4) Next season: plant cowpea early (at the start of the rains) to avoid the peak aphid period. Resistant varieties like 'IT90K-277-2' are available from IITA. Do not worry — cowpea aphids are manageable with these methods.
source: CSIR-SARI Cowpea Production Guide, 2023; reviewed by Dr. S. Adjei, entomologist

question: Daalunu. Akwukwo cassava m nwere akara mosaic, osisi anaghị eto nke ọma. Gịnị ka m ga-eme?
answer: Ọrịa ị na-ahụ bụ Cassava Mosaic Virus (CMD) — ọrịa kachasị njọ nke na-awakpo akpu. Ọ bụ whitefly na-ebute ya. O dighi ogwu ogwu — mgbochi ka mma. Ihe ị ga-eme: (1) Wepu osisi ndị na-arịa ọrịa ma kpochapu ha ozugbo — ejila ha mee kompositi. (2) Tinye osisi ohuru di iche iche na-eguzogide CMD dị ka TME 419 ma ọ bụ TMS 98/0581. (3) Gbaa mbọ hụ na ị na-achịkwa whiteflies — lee usoro whitefly na agri-001. (4) Ejila okpukpu ma ọ bụ mkpu site na osisi ndị na-arịa ọrịa. (5) Gbanwee ala — akụla akpu n'otu ala ahụ ruo oge abụọ. Nye akpu gị nri ọma site na itinye compost ma ọ bụ potaịsh ka osisi wee guzogide ọrịa. Maka enyemaka ọzọ, gakwuru ọrụ ugbo gị.
source: NRCRI Umudike Cassava Disease Guide; IITA Cassava Virology Lab

question: Witamwo. Mango yakwa irutaga nyeki ndune na matunda makamaga na goro. Ndingakora atia?
answer: Nyeki iria uonaga ni nyeje (Bactrocera dorsalis). Itumaga mango ikahiu na goro, na thukuna iria titumaga goro. Ndungata iria: (1) Ona macio mothe marĩ thi. (2) Thondeka mitego iria itagaga nyeki — tunya ndibei (methyl eugenol) na ke ndiria uthua. (3) Ute njege ikahi. (4) Tema na mutu macio marĩ thi, no utikie moto. (5) Wiki irayo, haya moto iria ikaa goro — mathondeko nyeje. (6) Agriria: harambia mitego (pheromone trap) kana matu 10. (7) Kana nyeki nyingĩ, thi na kïrîma na tiri — thi ikuragia nyeje. (8) Kwa mbere ya mwaka mũka: thondeka nyeje itathondeka — tega mango ciamo ciaku thi. (9) Tomia macio maku — nyeje itendaga kũgura mothondekeni. (10) Kana ũkĩona manyeki mongĩ, hoera KALRO kana ministry of agriculture.
source: KALRO Mango Production Guide; ICIPE Fruit Fly Management Brief

question: Sat sri akal. Mere moongphali de pate te gol gol chitthe lag gaye ne. Ki karan hai ate ki ilaaj hai?
answer: Ji, moongphali de patte te gol gol chitthe — iq kaga di bimari hai jo 'early leaf spot' kehlondi hai (Cercospora arachidicola). Eh fungus bimari hai jo pattiyon nu peela kar ke gira dindi hai, jo fasal de jhambe nu ghat dindi hai. Ilaj: (1) Bimari pattiyaan nu tor ke khet toh bahar kadh ke sutt deo (jalao nahi, balke mitti vich dafna deo). (2) Fungicide spray karo — chlorothalonil ya tebuconazole 2-3 gram prati litre paani vich. 10-14 din de antar naal 3 vaar chidakav karo. (3) Vadi bimari ho tan last spray to baad 14 din da wait karke hi vaddi karo. (4) Agle season vich roti de sake ta joth lagao — do saal tak moongphali usi khet vich na lagao. (5) Resistant variety variete lagao jivein 'ICGV 91114' ya 'Punjab 1'. (6) Saaf-suthra beej hi lagao — beej nu thiram fungicide naal treat karke lagao. (7) Phaslan vich haddi da powder paao ta ke potash di kami na hove.
source: Punjab Agricultural University Groundnut Guide; ICRISAT groundnut pathology

question: Oga. My cocoa pod dey turn black, and I fit see white something dey cover am like flour. The pod dey rot inside. Wetin cause am?
answer: Wetin you dey see na black pod disease (Phytophthora megakarya) — na the most serious cocoa disease for West Africa. E fit destroy up to 80% of your harvest if you no act. Wetin to do: (1) Harvest every pod wey don turn black or get white powder — remove them from the tree AND pick them from the ground. Carry them far from the farm and bury them deep (30 cm). (2) Spray copper-based fungicide (copper hydroxide or copper oxychloride at 4g per litre of water). Spray the whole tree, especially the pods. Repeat every 14 days during the rainy season. (3) Prune your cocoa trees — remove lower branches and thin the canopy so sunlight and air fit enter. Wet pods dry faster this way. (4) Maintain shade — too much shade dey keep the pods wet and help the fungus. Remove some shade trees if necessary. (5) Next season: plant tolerant varieties if available from CRIN or your extension agent. Regular harvesting (every 7-10 days during peak season) reduces the number of pods that get infected. No use fungicide wey expire — check the date before you buy.
source: CRIN Cocoa Disease Control Guide; IITA Cocoa Pest Management Brief, 2024

question: Eku oo, mo ri pe awon ewe cassava mi ti n ti n di ofeefee, won si ni awon eebi funfun kekere nisale ewe. Kini ohun ti mo le se lati ko won lo?
answer: This is cassava whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). Do NOT spray broad-spectrum insecticides — they kill beneficial insects and make the problem worse. Immediate steps: (1) Remove and burn the worst-affected leaves. (2) Plant sunn hemp or marigold as a border crop — whiteflies avoid them. (3) If more than half the plants are infested, apply neem oil at 5ml per litre of water, spraying ONLY under the leaves, once every 7 days for 3 weeks. (4) Introduce natural predators like ladybird beetles if available in your area.

question: Ina fama da matsalar maize ta. Ganyayyakin sun are showing signs of aflatoxin. Taya zan magance wannan?
answer: Mouldy or discoloured grains with a bitter taste are signs of aflatoxin contamination — a toxic fungus (Aspergillus flavus) that can cause liver damage in humans and animals. WARNING: Do NOT eat or sell mouldy grain. It is dangerous. Prevention for this season: (1) Dry harvested grain immediately to below 13% moisture. (2) Sort and remove all discoloured/mouldy grains by hand. (3) Store in clean, dry containers with good air circulation. (4) Use hermetic (sealed) storage bags if available — they cut off oxygen and stop fungal growth. For next season: plant resistant varieties, control insects that damage grain and create entry points for fungus, and harvest early at the right maturity.
